experiments.name: Local closed-loop smoke
experiments.hypothesis: Can the complete collect→cluster→allocate→verify→train→reevaluate loop execute reproducibly?
experiments.setup: Local synthetic environment; deterministic state-based graders; fixed seed.
experiments.result: The end-to-end loop executed and emitted trajectories, clusters, allocations, verified tasks, corrections, metrics and manifests.
experiments.interpretation: The system was executable, but success alone was insufficient to characterize what changed in the failure distribution.
experiments.next_decision: Add longitudinal failure-frontier instrumentation rather than only aggregate success.

experiments.name: Chromium browser fixture
experiments.hypothesis: Does the environment abstraction survive a real browser DOM/action loop?
experiments.setup: 12 isolated Chromium tasks using the retained browser fixture and state-based grading.
experiments.result: 58.3% task success; 54 failure events; 27 recovery attempts; all attempted recoveries succeeded. Token/cost coverage remained unknown rather than fabricated.
experiments.interpretation: The browser path was real enough to expose trajectories and recovery, but far too narrow for a scientific computer-use claim.
experiments.next_decision: Keep it as engineering evidence; require independent real-site tasks for paper-scale claims.

experiments.name: Moving failure-frontier smoke
experiments.hypothesis: Can a policy update leave success unchanged while shifting reliability risk?
experiments.setup: Local closed-loop smoke with mechanism matching across updates.
experiments.result: At iteration 2, task success stayed at 0.90 while risk introduced (0.5949) exceeded risk removed (0.4485), displacement ratio 1.3263.
experiments.interpretation: Aggregate success hid an adverse redistribution of failure risk.
experiments.next_decision: Promote risk displacement and mechanism transition states to core SORELIA outputs.

experiments.name: Fixed-budget curriculum comparison
experiments.hypothesis: Does frontier-aware allocation dominate simpler curricula under equal verified-data budgets?
experiments.setup: Same base policy, optimization path, eval set and verified training-data budget; compare SORELIA, static priority, frequency, random, difficulty and human-balanced.
experiments.result: In the retained v0.8 smoke, SORELIA did not win: human-balanced had best IID success (99.07%); frequency had best stress success (96.30%).
experiments.interpretation: The toy harness does not support a SORELIA superiority claim. Equal-budget controls are necessary because plausible simpler baselines remain strong.
experiments.next_decision: Retain null/adverse results and move superiority claims behind real-agent experiments.

experiments.name: Repeated-trial / multiseed inference
experiments.hypothesis: Are apparent differences stable under repeated stochastic evaluation?
experiments.setup: Repeated task trials across multiple seeds with paired bootstrap and paired randomization tests.
experiments.result: Small retained runs produced mixed effects and intervals that often included zero; no stable advantage was established.
experiments.interpretation: Single-draw agent evaluation was too brittle for claims.
experiments.next_decision: Make repeated trials and paired inference mandatory in paper-scale protocol.

experiments.name: Shifted stress split
experiments.hypothesis: Do conclusions survive a deterministic harder/longer perturbation split?
experiments.setup: IID and shifted/stress split with increased difficulty, horizon and perturbation intensity.
experiments.result: Methods changed ordering between IID and stress metrics; frequency led stress success in the retained v0.8 single-seed smoke while human-balanced led IID.
experiments.interpretation: A single IID aggregate can hide robustness differences. The stress split is useful plumbing but not real website-family OOD.
experiments.next_decision: Keep separate stress metrics and require held-out real environments before ecological-generalization claims.

experiments.name: Exploration ablation
experiments.hypothesis: Does reserving exploration budget reliably improve the adaptive curriculum?
experiments.setup: Full SORELIA vs no-exploration ablation under the same local harness.
experiments.result: In retained toy runs, removing exploration sometimes improved IID success; the effect was not monotonic.
experiments.interpretation: The intuitive "exploration always helps" hypothesis failed in the toy setting.
experiments.next_decision: Treat exploration ratio as an empirical hyperparameter and report ablation, not a default virtue.

experiments.name: Semantic negative controls
experiments.hypothesis: Does the method depend on meaningful failure labels/clusters?
experiments.setup: Shuffled failure labels and random cluster assignment, alongside full SORELIA and static priority.
experiments.result: In v0.9 smoke, random clusters and static priority outperformed full SORELIA on IID success; shuffled labels also remained competitive.
experiments.interpretation: Toy task structure may provide enough non-semantic signal that the current environment cannot establish causal value of semantic mechanism tracking.
experiments.next_decision: Require stronger real-agent tasks and retain negative controls as a falsification gate.

experiments.name: Matching ambiguity audit
experiments.hypothesis: Are cross-round mechanism identities certain enough to be treated as ground truth?
experiments.setup: Optimal bipartite matching with similarity margins and ambiguity flags.
experiments.result: The v0.9 integrity run reported 25% ambiguous matches; a later local frontier example reported 50% ambiguity among matched mechanisms.
experiments.interpretation: Automatic mechanism identity is not validated ground truth.
experiments.next_decision: Generate blank human calibration packets and block validated-identity claims until independent annotations exist.
